description.narrative: CAFOD will be leading the project in consortium with Christian Aid. The bulk of the project will utilize CAFOD’s capacity strengthening tools, expertise and will be managed from CAFOD’s office in Juba. Christian Aid will take up a key support function, delivering workshops on peer-to-peer learning as well as the midterm and final evaluation meetings. The Project Partner Ownership of the Capacity Strengthening: CAFOD and CA will promote partners’ ownership and agency of capacity strengthening through a process that is built on mutual trust, respect and clarity of purpose. From the onset of the project CAFOD and CA recognise every partner will have a unique nature with specific capacity priorities. We also recognise partners’ organisational improvement plans will have shared as well as specific organisational priorities. Thus, the project approach will ensure the capacity strengthening needs of all partners are addressed in both a coordinated as well as tailored manner, achieving value for money for the entire project implementation. Therefore, as the project develops the partners’ implementation plans will be further addressed through two broad categories: · Centrally coordinated capacity strengthening supports: Some commonly identified organisational priorities of the four partner organisations will be centrally coordinated by CAFOD for better efficiency. Partner Specific Capacity strengthening supports: partners that have capacity gaps specific to their respective organisations will be addressed separately, led by partners with the accompaniment and mentoring support of CAFOD
